section_1.title: The Prerequisite: The Metronome Pulse
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of a 'steady beat' as the fundamental unit of time. Explain that just as a heart beats, music relies on a consistent internal clock.
section_1.example: A mechanical frog sitting on a log, blinking its eyes exactly once per second to represent a steady beat.

section_2.title: Grouping the Beats: The Concept of the Bar
section_2.content: Explain that music needs organization. We group beats into 'measures' (or bars) using a strong downbeat to signal the start of a new cycle.
section_2.example: A row of 4 fireflies: the first one glows bright yellow (the '1' or downbeat), and the next three glow soft blue, creating a 4-beat cycle that repeats.

section_3.title: The Time Signature: The Mathematical Fraction
section_3.content: Translate musical notation into a visual fraction. The top number indicates how many beats per measure; the bottom number defines which note value receives one beat.
section_3.example: A visual animation of a '4/4' fraction appearing above a musical staff, where a 'pie chart' is sliced into 4 equal segments to show the measure's capacity.

section_4.title: Applying the Theory: Rhythmic Patterns
section_4.content: Show how different note durations (whole, half, quarter) must add up exactly to the total value allowed by the time signature.
section_4.example: A 'Music Tetris' game where the player must fit blocks (notes) into a frame (measure). If the measure is 4/4, a whole note block fills the entire space, while four quarter note blocks fill it perfectly.

section_5.title: Synthesis: The Living Measure
section_5.content: Summarize how measure theory acts as a grid that allows musicians to play together in perfect synchronization.
section_5.example: An orchestra of different cartoon animals (a lion on drums, a bird on flute) all playing from the same '4/4' grid; even though they play different notes, they all land on the '1' together.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
